readme.text:
How to read this file

• Rows = personas: Patient (mobile web), Staff (desk + doctor's room), Admin.
• P1 → P5 is the happy path. P6, P8 and P9 are the failure states most queue apps forget — they are designed, not left as errors.
• Every name, token and number is SAMPLE DATA for design only. It is NOT test evidence: Chapter 8 screenshots must be captured from the real build.
• Open decision drawn here as an assumption: alert delivery = browser push + SMS backup (PROJECT.md decision #3).

tA.text: Patient journey · mobile web, no app install

nP1.text: P1 answers the only three questions patients have: who is being served, how many are before me, can I leave? Wait time is a RANGE — one wrong minute value destroys trust. No full name on screen: anyone holding the QR link can open this page.

nP2.text: 10 ahead: calm tone (blue). The milestone track fills left-to-right so progress reads at a glance, even for low-literacy users. Same component as P1 — only the stage changes.

nP3.text: 5 ahead is the alert that must change behaviour, so it alone uses the warm colour and an explicit instruction: start heading back. Assumes patients stay within ~10 minutes of OPD.

nP4.text: 2 ahead: location-specific instruction (Waiting Area B, Room 3). If this page is not opened, the reminder repeats at 1 ahead — the PRD's 'patients miss alerts' mitigation.

nP5.text: Full-screen takeover, readable at arm's length. 'I'm on my way' tells the room the patient is coming and cuts premature no-shows. Optional — first thing to cut if MVP time runs short.

nP6.text: Missed turn is a recovery path, not an error message. The re-queue rule shown (one re-entry, after the current patient) is an ASSUMPTION — confirm with the clinic before building.

nP7.text: Two taps of feedback feed PRD §8 metrics directly: waiting experience, and 'did you step out?' — the only honest crowding-reduction signal without sensors. Fully skippable.

nP8.text: Offline: show last known state with its timestamp, never a blank page. Key reassurance: the queue only moves forward, so a stale count is the safe direction to be wrong in.

nP9.text: Tokens are valid for their day of issue only. An expired or tampered link points the patient to the desk instead of a dead end.

nS1.text: One sign-in for desk, room and admin roles; the role decides the landing screen. Counter or room is picked once per shift, not per action.

nS2.text: Built for speed at a crowded counter: a token in four fields plus Enter. The queue list shows each token's alert state, so staff can see who has already been warned before calling.

nS3.text: Right after creation the QR is shown large for the patient to scan at the counter. Patients without smartphones get the printed slip (S4) and the SMS backup.

nS4.text: 80 mm thermal slip, the common OPD counter printer. Token number first, QR second, three plain steps.

nS5.text: Every 'Call next' press drives every patient alert. If this button is not pressed on time the product fails — the PRD's 'delayed staff updates' risk. Hence one huge primary action and keyboard shortcuts.

nA1.text: Each KPI maps 1:1 to a PRD §8 success metric: idle wait, missed-turn rate, crowding (step-out share). Sample numbers only — real values come from the pilot.

nA2.text: Alert thresholds (10/5/2), grace period and re-queue rule are settings, not code — the clinic can tune them without a new release.
